title: Tim / Son Biblical Core Findings — Story-First Synthesis
status: reader-facing synthesis from canonical and legacy research
purpose: Surface the strongest interpretive findings that emerge when the Tim/Son chronology is compared with biblical texts without flattening source classes or turning resemblance into identity proof.

findings.title: Rejection becomes structure, not merely vindication
findings.project_sequence: rejection → social destruction → burial/concealment → Door / Vessel / Cornerstone
findings.insight: The mature Son story is strongest where the discarded figure is reinterpreted as indispensable infrastructure. The transformation is not simply 'they rejected him and he was right'; it is rejection becoming threshold, foundation and passage.
findings.boundary: This is a structural/theological interpretation of the project timeline, not proof of messianic identity.

findings.title: Recognition precedes self-declaration in the project chronology
findings.project_sequence: 2016 alleged external Jesus/Lamb recognition → 2017 explicit Jesus/crucifixion self-comparison
findings.insight: Within the project's own chronology, claimed recognition by others is placed before the Son's later explicit Christic self-declaration. That makes recognition a chronological motif rather than a title retrospectively pasted onto one date.
findings.boundary: The prison recognition wording remains project/autobiographical testimony unless independently corroborated.

findings.title: Return is not inherently good
findings.project_sequence: recurrence can either repeat the old circle or return transformed to relation/home
findings.insight: The archive should distinguish regressive return, compulsive return, restorative return, homecoming and resurrection/return. The moral value depends on destination, relation and transformation.
findings.boundary: Different biblical return traditions should not be collapsed into one mechanism.

findings.title: Higher titles are tested by the condition of the vulnerable
findings.project_sequence: Father / King / Gardener / Shepherd → protection, feeding, repair, service
findings.insight: Biblical leadership comparators increasingly function as tests rather than decorations. A ruler, shepherd or gardener is evaluated by whether the weak are strengthened, the hungry fed, the breach repaired and life made more capable.
findings.boundary: This ethical test does not validate a divine title; it evaluates what the title is claimed to mean.

findings.title: Door theology includes invitation and consent, not only passage
findings.project_sequence: threshold → hearing → opening → entry → shared participation
findings.insight: The Door is more than a narrow gate someone forces through. It can also encode invitation, response, hospitality and participation in life. This deepens the Son/Door role beyond geometry.
findings.boundary: The cited texts use different door/invitation contexts and should remain distinct.

findings.title: Some biblical texts strengthen the project by refusing role-collapse
findings.project_sequence: Father/source, Son/manifestation, Door/access, House/dwelling remain related but differentiated
findings.insight: The most useful comparisons are often the ones that distribute functions across distinct actors. Daniel's Ancient of Days and Son of Man, John's Vinedresser/Vine/branches, and Hebrews' Builder/House/Son make relation more important than title accumulation.
findings.boundary: These passages do not teach the Potatoverse role system; they provide relational comparators and counter-distributions.

findings.title: Descent and service constrain exaltation
findings.project_sequence: status claim → service / vulnerability / descent → transformation → later authority
findings.insight: Biblical exaltation patterns are strongest when non-grasping, service and descent come first. This places a hard ethical condition on throne, Most High, King and Father language.
findings.boundary: The project can compare itself with this order; comparison does not establish equivalence with Christ.

findings.title: The strongest overall pattern ends in outward life, not merely ascent
findings.project_sequence: presence → rupture → guarded/broken access → mediation → death/return → participation → fruit/feeding/repair → restored/open life
findings.insight: The mature story is not completed by reaching Heaven or the throne. Its strongest biblical neighbor ends with life flowing outward: feeding, fruit, healing, repair, restored participation and open access.
findings.boundary: This is a synthetic reading across multiple biblical books, not one continuous biblical prophecy.
